# Task: standard cell `o21ai`

Function: Y = !((A1 | A2) & B1)
Inputs: A1, A2, B1; output: Y; internal nets: n1, n2.
Supplies VPWR/VGND come from the template rails. The transistor netlist is fixed (from SkyWater sky130_fd_sc_hd).

Write the layout to `/o21ai.icl`, starting from this skeleton (keep the `pdk`, `param` and `device`
lines exactly; the block must be `stdcell o21ai`):
```icl
pdk sky130A
param WN=0.49 WP=0.75 WP2=0.52 L=0.15 H=2.72

stdcell o21ai width=<columns, your choice> height=H
  device M0 pmos w=WP l=L d=n1 g=A2 s=Y
  device M1 pmos w=WP2 l=L d=Y g=B1 s=VPWR
  device M2 nmos w=WN l=L d=n2 g=A1 s=VGND
  device M3 nmos w=WN l=L d=n2 g=B1 s=Y
  device M4 pmos w=WP l=L d=VPWR g=A1 s=n1
  device M5 nmos w=WN l=L d=VGND g=A2 s=n2
  <your geometry>
  port A1 in on=<a met1 shape>
  port A2 in on=<a met1 shape>
  port B1 in on=<a met1 shape>
  port Y out on=<a met1 shape>
end
```
Checked at the nominal parameters, then over the sweep: L=0.18 widths x1.0 H=2.72; L=0.25 widths x1.0 H=2.72; L=0.15 widths x0.85 H=2.72; L=0.15 widths x1.35 H=3.26; L=0.15 widths x1.9 H=4.08.
Choose `width` (columns of 0.46 um) large enough for L=0.25.

Verified layouts of similar cells (clean over the whole sweep) are in /examples/verified_a21oi.icl, /examples/verified_nand3.icl.

Never put the p row (`pd`, p-side contact li) into that max(): it pushes every gate contact up into the n-tap row (errors licon.14, var.*, licon.7, poly.2 and an LVS short of the inputs to VPWR). 2. Each gate contact sits ON its own gate: `gcX = contact licon cx=gX.cx bottom=cb` (shift by at most 0.1), `enclose gcX poly by=minx`, `enclose gcX li net=`. The poly pads are 0.33 wide, so neighbouring gates need a centre-to-centre pitch of at least 0.54 um. Place each gate from the previous one: `g2 = cross [nd, pd] poly w=L left=(g1.right + max(0.28, 0.54 - L))` (0.28 = room for a contact column; use max(0.21, 0.54 - L) for a series node without contact). 3. One `enclose [gc1, gc2, ...] npc` around all gate contacts. 4. Diffusion width = sum of the gaps + 2*0.265 end contacts + gates; derive it from L and the gaps so it follows the sweep. pdk sky130A
param WN=0.49 WP=0.75 L=0.15 H=2.72

stdcell a21oi width=6 height=H
  device M0 nmos w=WN l=L d=n1 g=A2 s=VGND
  device M1 pmos w=WP l=L d=n2 g=A1 s=VPWR
  device M2 pmos w=WP l=L d=Y g=B1 s=n2
  device M3 nmos w=WN l=L d=VGND g=B1 s=Y
  device M4 pmos w=WP l=L d=VPWR g=A2 s=n2
  device M5 nmos w=WN l=L d=Y g=A1 s=n1

  # stick plan (gate order A2 A1 B1; (net) = series node, no contact; | = break)
  #   p: n2 [A2] VPWR [A1] n2 [B1] Y |
  #   n: VGND [A2] (n1) [A1] Y [B1] VGND |
  ny0 = ptap.top + 0.27                 # bottom of the n row (diff-to-tap spacing)
  py1 = ntap.bottom - 0.27              # top of the p row
  span = 0.53 + 3*L + max(0.28, 0.54 - L) + max(0.28, 0.54 - L)
  x0 = cell.cx - span/2
  g1 = rect poly w=L left=(x0 + 0.265) yspan=(ny0 - 0.13, py1 + 0.13)   # gate A2
  g2 = rect poly w=L left=(g1.right + max(0.28, 0.54 - L)) yspan=(ny0 - 0.13, py1 + 0.13)   # gate A1
  g3 = rect poly w=L left=(g2.right + max(0.28, 0.54 - L)) yspan=(ny0 - 0.13, py1 + 0.13)   # gate B1
  nd1 = rect diff xspan=(g1.left - 0.265, g3.right + 0.265) yspan=(ny0, ny0 + WN)
  pd1 = rect diff xspan=(g1.left - 0.265, g3.right + 0.265) yspan=(py1 - WP, py1)
  nim = enclose [nd1] nsdm
  pim = enclose [pd1] psdm
  c1 = array licon in=nd1 left_of=g1
  c1l = enclose c1 li net=VGND
  c1s = strap li from=c1l to=vgnd_li
  c2 = array licon in=nd1 right_of=g2
  c2l = enclose c2 li net=Y
  c3 = array licon in=nd1 right_of=g3
  c3l = enclose c3 li net=VGND
  c3s = strap li from=c3l to=vgnd_li
  c4 = array licon in=pd1 left_of=g1
  c4l = enclose c4 li net=n2
  c5 = array licon in=pd1 right_of=g1
  c5l = enclose c5 li net=VPWR
  c5s = strap li from=c5l to=vpwr_li
  c6 = array licon in=pd1 right_of=g2
  c6l = enclose c6 li net=n2
  c7 = array licon in=pd1 right_of=g3
  c7l = enclose c7 li net=Y
  cb = max(nd1.top + 0.19, c1l.top + 0.25, c2l.top + 0.25, c3l.top + 0.25)
  gc1 = contact licon cx=g1.cx bottom=cb
  gp1 = enclose gc1 poly by=minx
  gl1 = enclose gc1 li net=A2
  gc2 = contact licon cx=g2.cx bottom=cb
  gp2 = enclose gc2 poly by=minx
  gl2 = enclose gc2 li net=A1
  gc3 = contact licon cx=g3.cx bottom=cb
  gp3 = enclose gc3 poly by=minx
  gl3 = enclose gc3 li net=B1
  gn = enclose [gc1, gc2, gc3] npc
  well y=((max(nd1.top) + 0.34 + min(pd1.bottom) - 0.18) / 2)
  a1m = contact mcon in=gl2
  a1p = enclose a1m m1 by=0.06 net=A1
  port A1 in on=a1p
  a2m = contact mcon in=gl1
  a2p = enclose a2m m1 by=0.06 net=A2
  port A2 in on=a2p
  b1m = contact mcon in=gl3
  b1p = enclose b1m m1 by=0.06 net=B1
  port B1 in on=b1p
  port Y out                       # pin goes on the routed met1 of Y
  route Y layers=m1,m2 prefer=m2
  route n2 layers=m1,m2 prefer=m2
end

# ICL — one layout language, four libraries (SKY130)

ICL lets you lay out SKY130 circuits at the level of abstraction the task needs, and
checks every result with signoff tools (magic DRC + netgen LVS). One syntax, one rule
engine, one router; the block type selects the library:

| block       | library      | level | you write                                                        |
|-------------|--------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `stdcell`   | `geom`       | 1     | shapes defined relative to other shapes (`enclose`, `right_of`, `cross`, `min`) |
| `cell`      | `assembly`   | 2     | PCell devices + placement relations + matching patterns          |
| `floorplan` | `floorplan`  | 3     | finished blocks (ICL cells or PDK std cells), DRC-aware spacing  |
| any block   | `route`      | 4     | auto/manual routing with width, spacing, symmetry, shielding, R, coupling |

A cell built at one level is instantiated by the next (`inst`), across files (`import`).

## The loop

```bash
bin/icl check  f.icl --top CELL     # compile + magic DRC + extract + netgen LVS + route report
bin/icl inspect f.icl --top CELL    # objects, positions, proximity, routes, warnings (text)
bin/icl build  f.icl --top CELL     # GDS + reference SPICE + PNG only
```
Exit code **0 = clean**, 1 = DRC/LVS/constraint violation, 2 = compile/route error.
`--json` gives a machine-readable report. Outputs go to `build/<file>/`
(`CELL.gds`, `CELL.ref.spice`, `CELL.extracted.spice`, `CELL.lvs.txt`, `CELL.png`).
Every error names the source line and usually suggests the fix; act on the hint.

## Common syntax

```
pdk sky130A
import "other.icl"
<block> <name> key=value ...
  [<name> =] <verb> <arg> <arg> ... <key>=<value> ...
end
```
* Values are expressions in **µm**: `0.5`, `0.5um`, `200nm`, `min`, `min+0.1`, `(x, y)`,
  `[a, b]`, `+ - * /`, `max(a,b)`, `grid(c, r)`, and references: `nd.top`, `M1.d.x`,
  `AMP.OUT`, `MT.cx`. Objects expose `left right bottom top cx cy w h`; devices expose pins
  `d g s`; instances expose their ports.
* `min` always means "the design-rule minimum for the layers involved".
* Nets are plain names; a net used once triggers a *dangling — did you mean* warning.
* Value bindings: `dw = 2*L + 0.81` (or `cb = max(nd.top + 0.19, snl.top + 0.25)`) on its own line
  inside a block names a value for later expressions.
* Parameters: `param WN=0.52 L=0.15 H=2.72` at file level (before the blocks); use them in any
  expression (`w=WN`, `height=H`, `w=(L + 0.53)`); override from the command line with
  `bin/icl check f.icl --param WN=0.84 --param H=3.26`. Write cells so they stay clean when the
  parameters change: derive positions from other shapes and from the parameters, and use
  `max(...)` when two rules both limit a position.
* Ports: `port <net> in|out|inout|power|ground` (+ `side=left|right|top|bottom layer=m2` in
  cells/floorplans to put the pin on an edge;

tap <name> kind=ptap|ntap net=<net> [cols=]
guardring <name> around=[o, ...] kind=ptap|ntap net=<net> [space=]
```
* `gap=min` placement is rule-aware compaction over every layer (diff, poly, implants,
  wells, li, metals). An explicit `gap=` below the legal minimum is an error naming the rule.
* Pattern letters map to the listed devices in order (A, B, ...); each device's `nf` must
  equal its letter count. Source/drain columns are solved automatically (neighbours share a
  column where they have a common net; where they cannot - e.g. two cascodes with different
  sources - the diffusion is broken there automatically, fewest breaks); gate straps go above
  or below the diffusion so interleaved devices never short. Dummies: gate to the body supply,
  source/drain tied to the neighbouring column. A non-centroid `common_centroid` pattern is
  reported.
* A cell needs a `ground` port if it has nmos devices and a `power` port if it has pmos devices.
* Wells and implants are merged automatically (n-wells closer than 2.8 µm become one well unless
  n-devices sit in between); every pmos n-well island must contain an `ntap`
  (tap or guard ring) and there must be a `ptap` — missing ties are errors with a fix.
* Placement of guard rings checks clearance and tells you how much room to leave.
See `examples/l2_analog.icl` (matched OTA; symmetric differential stage with guard rings).

## Level 3 — `floorplan` (library floorplan)

```
floorplan <name> [width=<um> height=<um>] [route_grid=0.23]
  inst <name> <cell | pdk:sky130_fd_sc_hd__inv_2> <port>=<net> ...      (alias: block)
  place / pair / mirror / move       as in cells
  proximity <A> <B>                  report: abut legal?, minimum legal gap + binding rule,
                                     layers on the facing edges and their distance to the edge
  port <net> <dir> side=<edge> layer=m3
```
`place B right_of=A` (gap=min) **abuts** B to A when every facing layer either keeps its
spacing or merges legally (same well/implant, same-net rails); otherwise B goes to the
smallest legal gap and the binding rule is recorded (`icl inspect` → `proximity:` lines).
PDK std cells (`pdk:` prefix) come with their real GDS and SPICE; their bodies (VPB/VNB)
connect to the supplies and need a tap cell abutted (`pdk:sky130_fd_sc_hd__tapvpwrvgnd_1`).
Chip routing defaults to met1–met3. See `examples/l3_chip.icl`.
```

route * [layers=...]                               defaults for all other nets
route <A> <B> symmetric axis=<x>                   B is routed as the exact mirror of A
wire  <net> layer=<m> [width=] path=[<pin|point>, (x, y), ...]     manual, checked, via stacks added

**What was hard:** The main challenge was getting the diffusion island breaks and net labels right for this AOI21 structure. The key insight was that gate order A1-A2-B1 works for both rows, but the n-row needs an island break between A2 and B1 (since M5's drain=VGND can't share diffusion with M3's source=Y). This required a 0.80 gap between g2 and g3, with nd2 covering only g3. The p-row stays as a single island VPWR-A1-n1-A2-Y-B1-VPWR. Getting the contact net labels correct on both sides of each gate (especially the Y net appearing on both sides of g2 on the p-row, and n2 on both sides of g1 on the n-row) was critical for LVS to match.
